For a customer at this stage (mid-market platform with clear expansion potential) we can offer:
- A one-time operational credit equal to 20% of the first-month committed spend if the close slips more than two weeks; OR
- A 30-day pilot extension with the current pricing and no additional onboarding fees.

I recommend the pilot extension in this case — it preserves revenue transparency for procurement and is easier to approve. If procurement pushes hard for a firm close date, we can do the credit but require a signature on the revised SOW.

Also suggest we document a phased acceptance:
1) Deliver logging artifact + sample logs (acceptance: sample ingestion into their SIEM).
2) Security review session (walkthrough and remediation plan).
3) Final sign-off (close).

I can draft the customer-facing MAP wording for the extension and the acceptance checklist.

Ellen / Procurement team —

Thanks for flagging the security audit — we’ve reviewed internally and propose the following path to keep momentum:

Summary (proposal)
- Provisional target close: 2026-11-18. This preserves procurement timelines while giving us space to complete the audit artifacts.
- Short-term deliverables (within 7 business days):
  1) Request-level logging artifact + sample logs for auth and inference paths (acceptance: sample ingestion into AtlasCloud SIEM).
  2) Technical review session (Redwood + AtlasCloud security) — suggested window: Wed, Nov 3.
- Contingency: MAP includes a one-time 14-day contingency extension. If used, Redwood will either extend the pilot by 30 days at current rates OR apply a one-time operational credit equivalent to 20% of the first-month committed spend (your choice at time of contingency).

Risk log highlights
- Primary risk: additional findings from audit requiring code-level change (mitigation: we scoped delivery to configuration & logging docs first; engineering triage for code fixes if needed).
- Acceptance dependencies: SIEM ingestion proof, security walk-through, procurement sign-off on revised SOW if credit requested.

Next steps
1) Confirm Nov 18 as provisional close (or propose alternate firm date).
2) Confirm availability for the technical review on Nov 3 (Laura will coordinate).
3) Confirm whether Procurement prefers pilot extension vs. credit as contingency.

I attached the updated MAP and current risk log for reference. Please let me know if you want any changes; Marissa can update the customer-facing wording based on procurement's preference.
